subject: SentryHealth pilot: stakeholder map, procurement asks, and exception request
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Ravi Shah <ravi.shah@sentryhealth.com>, Elena Morozova <elena@sentryhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 24 Jan 2027 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: SentryHealth pilot: stakeholder map, procurement asks, and exception request

Hi Ravi / Elena — great call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

1) Stakeholder map (as discussed)
   - Economic buyer: Elena Morozova (Head of Product) — will own pilot success metrics
   - Procurement / Legal: procurement@sentryhealth.com (Emily on vendor side) — purchase order + contract redlines
   - Security: Ravi to coordinate SOC 2 evidence and the security questionnaire we attached
   - Implementation: QA and Data Ops (two engineers inline) for the 6-week pilot

2) Decision criteria you shared
   - 1) Model relevance to triage suggestions (F1 on labeled set)
   - 2) Average inference latency under 150ms at 8-concurrent streams
   - 3) Observability and audit logs for each inference call

3) Immediate next steps (we propose):
   - We’ll send a pilot SOW + draft SLA (attached). Please confirm acceptance of the timeline by EOD Tue 1/26.
   - Security: completed questionnaire attached — Ravi, please confirm any gaps by Mon 1/25 so we can scope mitigations.
   - Procurement asks: they requested a pilot discount and SLA variance; we need internal approval for a 10% pilot discount and temporary SLA variance for logging retention in the pilot window.

Ask of you: confirm the technical contacts (names + emails) for implementation so we can schedule kickoff.

Attachments: Sentry_Security_Questionnaire.pdf, SLA_Draft_v2.docx

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0116

Thanks Lauren — good summary. Quick clarifications from procurement side: 

- Procurement wants to see the pilot SOW and the SLA before approving any discount. They typically process pilot PO requests in 5 business days once SOW/SLA are final.
- Two asks: (1) Can Redwood accept a PO with net-45 payment terms for the pilot? (2) On the SLA, we need a clause that limits our liability for PHI processing — can you confirm Redwood’s stance?

Also, security will review the attached questionnaire — I’ll flag any must-have mitigations by Monday.

Ravi
Head of Security Operations | SentryHealth
ravi.shah@sentryhealth.com

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 24 Jan 2027 17:05:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: SentryHealth pilot: stakeholder map, procurement asks, and exception request 

Team — forwarding the SentryHealth thread. Key asks that need internal alignment / approvals: 

1) Discount: procurement will likely push for pilot pricing reduction. I’m proposing a 10% one-time pilot discount (term limited to 6 weeks, non-recurring) to help unblock procurement. Approval needed from Revenue Ops / Sales Manager.
2) Payment terms: procurement asked net-45 for the pilot. Standard is net-30 — need sign-off from finance for net-45. If we can’t do net-45, can we accept PO and invoice on net-30 but accelerate onboarding?
3) SLA / liability clause: procurement is asking for explicit PHI liability language and a logging retention variance. Security (Stephanie) — they may request that logs be stored in their EU region for that pilot cohort; SentryHealth is US-based but asked about regional retention in the questionnaire.
4) Security questionnaire: they attached responses; Stephanie, please triage. Any gaps that trigger a security exception? If so, we’ll need a signed security exception with mitigation steps for the pilot.

Proposed internal decision: approve 10% pilot discount and allow a temporary SLA variance limited to the pilot (30 days post-pilot auto-revert), conditional on Security sign-off and Finance acceptance of net-45 or deposit. 

Can you reply with approvals / blockers by EOD Monday 1/25?

—
Lauren

---

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 25 Jan 2027 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: SentryHealth pilot: stakeholder map, procurement asks, and exception request

Lauren — I’m okay to approve the 10% pilot discount for this account. We should mark it as a "pilot incentive" in the CRM and ensure the discount is non-recurring.

On net-45: I don’t want to set a wider finance precedent for net-45 on pilot deals. Two pragmatic options: (1) ask for a 25% upfront deposit on net-45; or (2) accept net-30 and offer a one-time onboarding acceleration which shortens time-to-value. Which would Sentry prefer?

Stephanie — please flag any security conditions we must require before enabling pilot access. If security needs a formal exception, route to Legal with required mitigation language.

Ben
Senior Director, Sales | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, marissa_coole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 25 Jan 2027 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: SentryHealth pilot: stakeholder map, procurement asks, and exception request

Thanks — reviewed the questionnaire (see attached). Two security items to call out: 

1) Logging retention / regional residency: Sentry has asked for logs to be retained in their preferred US region but also asked about EU residency as a potential later requirement. For the pilot, we can permit a logging-retention variance limited to 90 days, with logs stored in US-East. We require encrypted transports (TLS 1.3) and customer KMS integration for any persisted artifacts. This will be documented as a time-limited security exception.

2) PHI liability clause: Our standard contract excludes indemnity for customer-handled PHI. Legal will need to review a tightened clause if Sentry insists. We can accept limited PHI handling for the pilot if: (a) they sign a DPA addendum, (b) we scope the dataset so Redwood’s processing is transient (no long-term storage), and (c) they accept the logging retention exception above.

If Ben approves the pilot discount, I’ll prepare the security exception memo and circulate to Legal. Otherwise, I need a clear yes/no on whether we should allow a net-45 deposit model or insist on net-30 with deposit.

—
Stephanie Nguyen
Security & Compliance Manager | Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Ravi Shah <ravi.shah@sentryhealth.com>, Elena Morozova <elena@sentryhealth.com>
Cc: procurement@sentryhealth.com, ben_carter@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 26 Jan 2027 11:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SentryHealth pilot: stakeholder map, procurement asks, and exception request

Ravi / Elena — thanks for the quick turnaround. 

Internal update: Sales is approving a one-time 10% pilot discount (non-recurring). Finance would prefer net-30, but we can accept a net-45 with a 25% upfront deposit to mitigate credit risk — would that work for Sentry?

Security is comfortable with a time-limited logging retention variance (90 days in US-East) and requires a DPA addendum plus customer KMS for persisted artifacts. We’ll include the security exception memo with mitigations in the SOW appendices. Legal will review PHI language if you need tightened indemnity.

Next steps: 
 - Ravi / Elena: confirm whether Sentry will do the 25% deposit with net-45 or accept net-30 by EOD 1/27 so we can finalize SOW and issue PO instructions.
 - Procurement: once terms confirmed, we’ll send final SOW + DocuSign link (preview attached).

If that works, I’ll route the signed exception memo to Legal and Finance and schedule a kickoff for 2/1.

Thanks — Lauren

Attachments: SLA_Draft_v2.docx, Sentry_Security_Questionnaire.pdf
